classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the second acute angle is also 45°, infer equal legs, then use Pythagoras and substitute the side lengths into the three taught ratios. The requested sequence guides these routine connections.

content.prompt: Draw a right-angled triangle with an angle of $45^\circ$. If one of the shorter sides has length 1, write down the lengths of the other sides without using trigonometry. Hence find the exact values of $\sin45^\circ$, $\cos45^\circ$ and $\tan45^\circ$.

answer.short:
The other sides have lengths $1$ and $\sqrt2$ units. $\sin45^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt2}$, $\cos45^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and $\tan45^\circ=1$.

The shorter sides are equal; use Pythagoras' theorem for the hypotenuse.
answer.worked:
The third angle is $45^\circ$, so the triangle is isosceles and both shorter sides have length 1. Let the hypotenuse have length $h$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=1^2+1^2\\h^2&=2\\h&=\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Using opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to either $45^\circ$ angle:
$$\begin{align*}\sin45^\circ&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\\cos45^\circ&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\\tan45^\circ&=\frac11=1\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Completed isosceles right triangle with the requested angle and all side lengths.
spec.mathematics: Legs 1 and 1; hypotenuse sqrt(2); reference angle 45 degrees.
